_comment: EDIT profile_brief AND the keyword weights TO MATCH YOUR OWN CV. Everything here is an example tuned for a mid-level AWS/Terraform DevOps engineer - it will score badly for anyone else. The rule score is a SCREEN, not a verdict: it ranks candidates and decides who is worth an LLM call. Measured against real LLM scores on 7 jobs, mean absolute error was ~2.4 points: good enough to rank, not good enough to trust alone.
_profile_brief_comment: The ONLY thing the model is told about you. Keep it under ~200 words - it is sent on every judged run, so length costs tokens. Be explicit about what you DO NOT have: the 'ABSENT' list is what makes the model reject plausible-looking mismatches. Replace this entirely.
profile_brief: EXAMPLE - REPLACE ME. DevOps/Cloud Engineer, 4.5 yrs. Core: AWS (ECS/EC2/Lambda/RDS/S3/IAM/CloudWatch), Terraform, CI/CD (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps), Docker, Python, Bash. Strong: OIDC keyless CI auth, IAM least-privilege, DevSecOps scanning, cloud cost/FinOps, Linux, Nginx. WORKING KNOWLEDGE ONLY (treat deep requirements as gaps): Kubernetes. ABSENT (hard gaps): Azure or GCP as primary cloud, Ansible/Chef/Puppet, deep K8s/OpenShift admin, Go/Java/.NET, data engineering, ML, SAP/Oracle/Salesforce, networking (BGP/Cisco/F5), L1/NOC support. Target band 3-7 yrs, sweet spot 3-6. Out of band: 0-2 yrs, 8+ yrs, Staff/Principal/Architect/Manager. Locations: <your cities>, or genuine remote.
_positive_cap_comment: Positive keywords are TABLE STAKES - nearly every posting in your field mentions your core stack. Summing them uncapped made every job score 10/10 and destroyed all ranking signal (measured). Capped, they only separate a relevant post from an irrelevant one; the negatives below do the actual discriminating.
_title_reject_comment: Substring match on the lowercased TITLE, applied BEFORE get_job_details, so a reject costs ZERO detail calls. Verified worth it: 'Staff Site Reliability Engineer' was the worst rule-score error (+5 vs the model) and this list catches it for free. Keep it CONSERVATIVE - it is a blacklist, not a ranking. Anything not obviously wrong must still get its body read, because titles mislead constantly.

cloud_primary._comment: Penalty when a cloud you do NOT know dominates the body (by mention count).

years._comment: Parsed only from figures qualified by 'of experience'. A bare number regex grabs incidentals like '1 year of free training' and reports a 3-7yr role as wanting 1 year (measured, then fixed).

kubernetes._comment: Example of grading a partial skill: penalise only when it reads as a hard requirement, not whenever it is mentioned. Adapt or delete for your own stack.

freshness._comment: Only score jobs posted within this window. WARNING: LinkedIn surfaces jobs unreliably - measured, two roles appeared a full DAY late because page-1 ordering reshuffled. Anything seen late is permanently invisible under a tight cap. Skipped jobs ARE listed in the shortlist so the loss is visible. 30 suits a 30-minute schedule and a hypercompetitive market; 90-120 is safer. Set enabled=false to score everything within max_posted_age_days.

saturation._comment: Applicant VELOCITY, not raw count. 20+ applicants within the first hour means the pool is already saturated; the same 20 over 24h is a cold posting worth applying to. Dropped before the LLM call, so they cost no tokens, and listed separately rather than hidden.

llm._comment: ONE call per run, only when there is something to judge. Set enabled=false for a fully offline, zero-token pipeline - you keep the rule scores but lose semantic catches, e.g. a posting titled 'Senior SRE' whose body reads 'not a standard QA, DevOps, or operational position' and is actually an ML role. No regex sees that.
